headline: South Korean regulators say suspected AI-agent cyberattacks have now hit 16 financial firms, more than double the seven first reported, exposing about 100,000 personal records.
score_reason: Kept at pool score 8: confirmed by the regulator, large consumer data exposure, growing count; wording stays 'suspected' as the article does.
importance_line: Customers of Korean banks, savings banks and crypto firms may have had names and national ID numbers exposed, and the regulator has found basic security gaps at 130 of 555 firms checked, though no account or card numbers are known to be taken.
summary: The Korea Times reports that South Korea's Financial Services Commission said on 14 Oct 2026 that suspected AI-agent-driven attacks have hit 16 financial firms, including Shinhan, KB Kookmin, BNK Busan and Hana banks, up from seven first reported, and exposed about 100,000 records such as resident registration numbers. This updates our 11 Oct 2026 coverage of AI tools used in attacks on South Korean banks: what is new is the larger count and the regulator's finding that 130 of 555 inspected firms, 23.4 percent, had security gaps such as missing patches, with reforms planned to hold CEOs and boards more accountable.
notes: Attacks are called 'suspected' AI-agent driven; the article does not say which AI tools were used.
